name: Space Shuttle Columbia
best_known_for: OV-102 — the first orbiter to fly to space. STS-1 (1981-04-12) opened the Shuttle era; lost on re-entry during STS-107 (2003-02-01) with all seven crew
credit: The first operational Space Shuttle orbiter. Rolled out 1979, first flight STS-1 with John Young + Robert Crippen on 1981-04-12 — also the first crewed test flight of a new American spacecraft in 25 years. Heaviest of the orbiters at ~80 t empty (carried the original heavy SILTS / instrumentation suite); never fitted with the lighter ALPHA Station-docking system, so never flew to Mir or ISS. Flew 28 missions including the 1990 Astro-1 UV-astronomy mission, the 1993 SLS-2 life-sciences flight, and Senator John Glenn's STS-95 return-to-space in 1998. Lost during re-entry on STS-107 (2003-02-01) — foam strike during launch breached the left wing's RCC leading edge; the vehicle disintegrated over Texas at Mach 18 with the loss of all seven crew (Husband, McCool, Anderson, Brown, Chawla, Clark, Ramon). The accident grounded the Shuttle fleet for 29 months and triggered the Vision for Space Exploration that led to Constellation + Artemis.

flights.flight_designation: STS-1 (1981-04-12) · first Space Shuttle flight; Young + Crippen — first crewed test of a new US spacecraft in 25 years
STS-9 (1983-11-28) · first Spacelab mission; first 6-person Shuttle crew; first non-US ESA payload specialist (Merbold)
STS-32 (1990-01-09) · retrieved LDEF (Long Duration Exposure Facility) after 5.7 years in orbit
STS-93 (1999-07-23) · deployed Chandra X-ray Observatory; first Shuttle commanded by a woman (Collins)
STS-107 (2003-01-16) · LOST on re-entry 2003-02-01 — foam strike breached the RCC left-wing leading edge; all 7 crew (Husband, McCool, Anderson, Brown, Chawla, Clark, Ramon) perished
